profile.reading:
Csquare IAD4-B sits at 21571 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147, one of two street addresses (21561 and 21571 Beaumeade Circle) Csquare's own spec sheet lists under its single "IAD4" campus heading. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists only one Virginia "IAD4_A" line item for the entire leased IAD4 campus, 58,939 square feet sellable, 77.8 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, rather than separately disclosing an "IAD4-B" line item; this building's existence and address are nonetheless confirmed independently by Csquare's own spec-sheet documentation and this record's own OSM sourcing. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet states a campus-wide 57,927 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with standard cage density up to 300 watts per square foot, and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor as a matter of public record.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, and Csquare's IAD4 campus sits among dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and separately discloses that the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked across this dataset.

profile.research_note: IAD4 campus power/sqft figures (57,927 sqft raised floor, 35.8MW utility, 16.8MW UPS, 20MW generator; SEC S-1 gives one combined "IAD4_A" line at 58,939 sqft) are published only campus-wide across the IAD4-A and IAD4-B buildings, not broken out per building, so no capacity/sqft figure was attributed to this specific row. Cage density of "up to 300 watts/sqft" is a ceiling, not stored as a typical density figure.

reading.body:
IAD4-B is one building within Csquare's IAD4 campus in Ashburn, Virginia, sharing 57,927 square feet of raised floor and a campus-wide utility power allocation of 35.8 megawatts across two co-located structures. The campus holds SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it to host workloads requiring financial transaction processing, payment card compliance, and federal security standards. Csquare publishes no individual capacity breakdown between IAD4-A and IAD4-B, so this specific building's power allocation cannot be stated.

At a 300-watt-per-square-foot ceiling density typical of cage colocation, the 57,927 square feet of raised floor could support approximately 17.4 megawatts of IT load at maximum build-out, though this is an upper bound and not Csquare's stated design figure. The 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity are published campus-wide; the campus appears configured for mixed workloads rather than the 40+ kilowatt per-rack densities typical of AI training clusters. Csquare does not name the power utility or publish a year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor.

Within Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities, IAD4 ranks 24th by published megawatts and represents one of only 23 facilities statewide with disclosed capacity figures. The facility sits in Ashburn's Data Center Alley, the world's largest data center concentration, where dozens of hyperscale and colocation operators compete within a few miles. Csquare's entire 64-facility portfolio across 21 markets holds 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity as of March 2026, placing this single campus as a minor component of a larger infrastructure operator born from Brookfield Infrastructure's 2024 consolidation of bankrupt and divested data center assets.
